summary: Karunesh Shukla worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation and held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, including Reader (attested 1973) and Professor and Head (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. She completed her studies, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later serving at the University of Bern as professor (1999) and dean (2007–2010).

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A.), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as Officiating Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1931), Deputy Director-General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944), and held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College (~1868–1872), president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1889–1893), and vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and later as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

Kasten Anders Rönnow specialized in Indology and religious studies, earning his Fil.kand. at Uppsala University under Jarl Charpentier. He later served as Acting Professor at Uppsala University (1928) and Lund University (1932–1933).

Katarzyna Marciniak is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Her academic career includes posts at the University of Warsaw as a postdoctoral researcher in the Research Centre of Buddhist Studies (attested 2016) and as adjunct (2020).

Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having earned her BA and D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. Her academic appointments include positions at SOAS, Visiting Professor at King's College London (-2022), and Professor of Buddhist Studies at Oxford (2022).

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Kupfer is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 1999–2000) and the University of Freiburg (attested 2000–2001).

Katharina Sabernig works in Tibetology and related fields. She earned an MD from the Medical University of Vienna (1997–2008) and a PhD from the University of Vienna (2007–2017), and holds a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katharine von Garnier-Moewes was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the University of Leipzig and earned her PhD from Heidelberg University (~1904–1907).
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, along with teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned an M.A. at the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. at McGill University. She became a professor at McGill University circa 1978.

Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1992). She was Assistant Professor at Northwestern (~1993–1995) and became Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2017.

Kathleen Gough was a scholar in archaeology and Indology who earned her Ph.D. at Girton College, Cambridge. She held posts at Brandeis, the University of Oregon, Simon Fraser University, and was an Honorary Research Associate at the University of British Columbia (1970).

Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher who earned her Ph.D. from Yale University. She became a Professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 1992 and held visiting fellowships at Bellagio Center (1993), Australian National University (1997), and Canberra School of Music (1997).
